entries.name: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
entries.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

entries.name: Scheduling in Queueing Systems with Uncertain and Evolving Holding Costs
entries.abstract: In queueing systems, the holding costs of jobs may evolve in uncertain ways. For example, in content moderation for social media platforms, the cost of delaying the review of a content piece is proportional to its view trajectory, which fluctuates and is a priori unknown. To capture such uncertain and evolving holding cost patterns, we consider a queueing model where job states evolve based on a Markov chain with state-dependent instantaneous holding costs. We demonstrate that in the presence of such uncertain and evolving holding costs, the two canonical algorithmic principles, instantaneous-cost ($cμ$-rule) and expected-remaining-cost ($cμ/θ$-rule), are suboptimal. By viewing each job as a Markovian ski-rental problem, we develop a new index-based algorithm, Opportunity-adjusted Remaining Cost (OaRC), that adjusts to the opportunity of serving jobs in the future when uncertainty partly resolves. We show that the suboptimality gap of OaRC scales as $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{N})$, where $N$ is the system size. This bound shows that OaRC achieves asymptotic optimality for overloaded systems when the system size $N$ scales to infinity. Moreover, the bound is independent of the state-space size, which is a desirable property when job states contain contextual information. We corroborate our results with an extensive simulation study based on two holding cost patterns (online ads and user-generated content) that arise in content moderation for social media platforms. Our simulations based on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that OaRC consistently outperforms existing practice, which is based on the two canonical algorithmic principles.

entries.name: The uncertainty of a tournament draw: Insights from the Champions League
entries.abstract: The group draw of major sports tournaments implies some uncertainty, with lucky teams often enjoying a substantial unfair advantage. For the first time in the literature, we propose a technique to quantify this draw uncertainty, which, arguably, should be minimised. Our simulation-based approach requires generating a representative set of random draws to compute the variance of qualifying probabilities for each team. The method is applied to compare draw uncertainty in the former group stage and the current incomplete round-robin league phase of the UEFA Champions League, under both accurate and inaccurate seedings. We also break down the impact of the 2024/25 reform into various components. The new format is found to decrease draw uncertainty, but the reduction is mainly attributable to the inaccurate seeding system used by UEFA. Consequently, the primary benefit of an incomplete round-robin tournament compared to the standard group stage lies in the robustness of its draw uncertainty to the seeding of the teams.

entries.name: On subradically sifted sums related to Alladi's higher order duality between prime factors
entries.abstract: In this paper, I utilize a variant of the Selberg--Delange method to find quantitative estimates of the sums \[M_{k,ω}(x,y)=\sum_{\substack{p_{1}(n)> y\\ n\leq x} } μ(n) {ω(n)-1\choose k-1},\] where $y$ can grow with $x$ but we must have $y\leq Y_0\exp(\mathscr{p}\frac{\log x}{(\log\log (x+1))^{1+ε}})$ with $Y_0,\mathscr{p},ε>0$. Moreover, I give preliminary upper bounds for the general range $1.9\leq y\leq x^{\frac{1}{k}}$. In addition, I formalize the notions of subradical and radical dominance and discuss their relevance to the analytic approach to the study of arithmetic functions. Lastly, I give a fascinating formula related to the derivatives of the gamma function and the Hankel contour, which should be relevant for those employing the Selberg--Delange method to obtain higher-order terms.

entries.name: Global smoothing of singular Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties
entries.abstract: We study the problem of smoothing Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties with isolated Du Bois (equivalently, log canonical) lci singularities. For Fano varieties, we show that any such $Y$ admits a deformation to a Fano variety with only $1$-rational singularities, and if $Y$ has only non-$1$-rational hypersurface singularities, then $Y$ is smoothable. For Calabi-Yau varieties, we show first that any such $Y$ deforms to a Calabi-Yau with only $1$-Du Bois singularities. Moreover, if $Y$ has only non-$1$-Du Bois hypersurface singularities then $Y$ is smoothable. Both smoothing statements extend to lci singularities satisfying suitable local conditions. When we allow a Calabi-Yau to have $1$-liminal singularities, a global condition is needed, which we express in terms of the Hodge-Du Bois numbers of $Y$. These theorems recover and generalize results for threefolds of Friedman, Namikawa, Namikawa-Steenbrink, Gross, and Friedman-Laza. In higher dimensions, our results provide alternative smoothing conditions and also extend the work of Friedman-Laza from the case of rational hypersurface singularities to Du Bois lci singularities.

entries.name: Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calderón problem
entries.abstract: We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calderón problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.

entries.name: Axioms for validity: from tests, e-values and p-values to decisions
entries.abstract: The emerging literature on hypothesis testing with data-dependent significance levels relies on a particular extension of the Type-I error. Existing arguments for this extension are heuristic. We show it is uniquely characterized by three axioms: law-invariance, agreement with classical testing on constant levels, and the preservation of (in)validity under independent selection of the level. We find that three analogous axioms characterize the e-value as a multi-decision generalization of a test. We also characterize the p-value, reducing the p-vs-e debate to a simple property: should independent selection among evidence variables that are invalid under the same null distribution be able to produce a valid evidence variable? Our main technical contribution is to show how e-values emerge in every decision problem with a notion of validity that satisfies law invariance, the independent selection axiom, and an axiom stating that a procedure that selects an invalid procedure with arbitrarily high probability must itself be invalid. We also extend recent results using e-values to support decision making to arbitrary evidence variables. In an application, we justify expectation-based error rates in multiple testing and recover the 'e-closure principle'.

entries.name: A high-order IMEX-DG solver for atmospheric dynamics: rotating tests on non-conforming meshes
entries.abstract: We present a high-order implicit-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (IMEX-DG) solver for the compressible Euler equations that accounts for rotational effects within an atmospheric framework. Time integration follows a second-order additive Runge-Kutta scheme, treating stiff acoustic modes implicitly and advective terms explicitly. The solver is built on the deal.II finite element library, combining matrix-free operator evaluation, adaptive non-conforming mesh capabilities, and distributed-memory parallelism. The inclusion of rotation extends the framework to large-scale atmospheric dynamics, where the Coriolis force plays a central role in geostrophic balance. Its incorporation into a high-order matrix-free DG discretisation is, however, non-trivial, as it requires a careful formulation of the discrete rotational operator. Two alternative treatments of the rotational and gravitational source terms within the solution strategy, based on nonlinear fixed-point iterations, are therefore introduced and compared in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. A discrete analysis of the rotational operator is also carried out in order to derive a formulation suitable for efficient matrix-free implementation. The proposed formulation is verified through convergence studies on rotating inertia-gravity wave benchmarks and further assessed in fully three-dimensional simulations of stratified flow over orography on both uniform and adaptive meshes. The numerical results show that the rotating IMEX-DG framework has the expected accuracy and stability properties while correctly capturing the asymmetry and wave structures induced by rotation in large-scale atmospheric flows.

entries.name: On $H=W$ in Banach function spaces
entries.abstract: In this paper we prove ``$H=W$" in the context of a Banach function space $X(Ω)$. Let $Ω$ be a subset of ${\mathbb R}^n$ and denote by $W^1_X(Ω)$ the collection of all those $f\in X(Ω)$ whose distributional derivatives $\partial_jf$ are contained in $X(Ω)$. Our main result provides a small collection of ``universal" hypotheses on $X(Ω)$ that ensure $W^1_X(Ω)$ is equal to $H^1_X(Ω)$, the formal closure of ${Lip}(Ω)\cap W^1_X(Ω)$ with respect to the norm \[\|f\|_{W^1_X(Ω)} = \|f\|_{X(Ω)} + \|\nabla f\|_{X(Ω)}.\] The main theorem has two corollaries. The first gives a slightly stronger set of hypotheses for ``$H=W$", and the second gives density of $C^\infty_c({\mathbb R}^n)$ in $W^1_X({\mathbb R}^n)$.

entries.name: Birational Algebraic Topology
entries.abstract: Over any qcqs scheme $S$, we show that inverting dense open immersions in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, $log\mbox{-}\mathcal{H}^\Box(S)$, and $\mathcal{P}_Σ(\mathrm{Sm}_S)$ yields the same birational $\infty$-category $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$. Unlike in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, all Nisnevich truncations and homotopy sheaves (including $π_0^{nis}$) of birational spaces remain birational, and hence $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is Postnikov complete. Moreover, the birational localization $L_{bir}$ commutes with the bar construction, ensuring effective delooping for every grouplike object in $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ and yielding an unstable birational higher-connectivity theorem. Building on these results, we establish birational analogs of the van Kampen theorem, the higher Galois theory of coverings, and the Freudenthal suspension theorem. When $S$ is geometrically unibranch with finitely many generic points, we show that $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is in fact an $\infty$-topos of homotopy dimension zero. Over a perfect field, we identify discrete birational group sheaves with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves whose $\mathbb{G}_m$-contraction vanishes, and deduce that $S^{2,1}$-nullification $L^{2,1}$ agrees with $L_{bir}$ on pointed $L^{2,1}$-connected spaces. Finally, over any field, we prove that $L_{bir}$ preserves generic values of $π_0^{\mathbb{A}^1}$ on motivic colimits of proper schemes; over perfect fields, it therefore detects their $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectivity and yields an equivalence $\mathbb{H}_0^{\mathbb{A}^1} \simeq \mathbb{H}_0^b$ for them, answering a question of Asok and Haesemeyer in greater generality.

entries.name: The number of composite class sizes in finite groups
entries.abstract: We consider finite groups with at least three conjugacy class sizes that are composite numbers and we prove that, in that situation, the number of prime class sizes is bounded by the number of composite class sizes. The analogous result for (non-)prime-power class sizes is also addressed.

entries.name: Non-vanishing uniqueness threshold for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation in dimension at least three
entries.abstract: We study the threshold for the existence of exactly one unbounded cluster for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$ for $d\geq 3$. By recent results of Grebík and Recke and d'Achille et al., this "uniqueness threshold" $p_u(λ)$ tends to zero as the intensity $λ$ of the underlying Poisson point process tends to zero, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation defined on an ambient space from a family of geometric spaces that includes Cartesian products $\mathbb{H}^{d_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb{H}^{d_k}$ with $k,d_1,\dots,d_k\geq 2$. In contrast, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$, Benjamini and Schramm have shown that $p_u(λ)$ tends to one as $λ$ tends to zero, and $p_u(λ)>1/2$ for all $λ>0$. An unpublished argument of D'Achille and Curien shows that for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, the uniqueness threshold satisfies $p_u(λ)\leq 1/2$ for all $λ>0$. Here we will show that $\inf_{λ>0}p_u(λ)>0$ for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$. This answers a question of Grebík and Recke. The ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is a random tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^d$ introduced recently by D'Achille et al. In a sense that can be made precise, it corresponds to the $λ\searrow 0$ limit of the Poisson-Voronoi tessellation. Via a minor adaptation of our proof, we are also able to show that the uniqueness threshold of the ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is strictly positive.

entries.name: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
entries.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linear elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

entries.name: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
entries.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

entries.name: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
entries.abstract: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

entries.name: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
entries.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support Kähler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

entries.name: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
entries.abstract: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.

entries.name: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
entries.abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $α\in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,α}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_δ$ for the closed $δ$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,α})_δ$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,α}(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_α$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < δ< 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_α)_δ$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_α(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $γ((E_α)_δ)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/δ))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, with constants depending only on $α$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_α)_δ$ is at most $C_αγ((E_α)_δ)^{2α}$ for every $0 < δ< 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $α> 1/2$, and its exponent $2α$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $α$ tends to one.

entries.name: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
entries.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a formula for the Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple determination of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even degree cohomology. This is then applied to the study of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we analyse the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,q}$ as well as ample divisor complements in orbifold K3 surfaces and Calabi-Yau threefolds, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

entries.name: On the $φ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
entries.abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $φ^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.

entries.name: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
entries.abstract: We prove that complete expanding Kähler--Ricci solitons with complete soliton fields characterize Steinness of relatively compact domains in complex manifolds, provided their closures admit neighborhoods with holomorphic immersions into Euclidean space. We construct canonical, instantaneously complete Kähler--Ricci flows from positive closed $(1,1)$-currents with global plurisubharmonic potentials and vanishing Lelong numbers. Nonzero currents homogeneous under a complete real holomorphic flow yield nontrivial expanders with prescribed soliton fields. We obtain a product criterion and uniformization results for balls and finite-type domains in complex surfaces. If $D$ is a relatively compact Stein domain in a reduced pure-dimensional Stein space of dimension at least two and $\operatorname{Sing} D$ is finite and nonempty, we prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{Reg} D)$ is compact, excluding nontrivial expanders with complete soliton fields.

entries.name: Interior $W^{2,p}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
entries.abstract: In this paper, we extend Caffarelli's interior $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ regularity theory for the Monge-Ampère equation to the $k$-Hessian equation, $3\leq k\leq n-1$, under sharp Sobolev or Hölder assumptions on the solution. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,β}$ for some $1-2/k<β<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1<p<\infty$; if the density is positive and belongs to $C_{\mathrm{loc}}^α$, then $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,α}$ for $0<α<1$. For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we also establish global $W^{2,1}$ regularity on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{1,1}$ domains with $C^{1,1}$ boundary values.

entries.name: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
entries.abstract: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.

entries.name: A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint
entries.abstract: We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.

entries.name: Quantitative thick-fiber property
entries.abstract: We introduce the quantitative thick-fiber property, an analogue of the Entov--Polterovich non-displaceable fiber theorem for maps whose coordinate functions need not Poisson commute. We prove that this property holds for closed symplectic manifolds admitting a suitable, not necessarily linear, functional on the space of continuous functions. Conversely, we establish an obstruction and show that the property fails for certain irrational symplectic four-tori and Kodaira--Thurston manifolds. These results reveal a new rigidity--flexibility distinction: whereas the Entov--Polterovich theorem gives a universal fiber-rigidity phenomenon, its quantitative counterpart holds on some closed symplectic manifolds and fails on others, thereby defining a new symplectic rigidity invariant. We also introduce the non-displaceability width of a continuous map, defined as the infimum of the radii for which a non-displaceable thick fiber exists, and use it to obtain quantitative obstructions to uniform approximation by maps with small Poisson brackets.

entries.name: A locally conservative LDG method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem
entries.abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem representing the interaction between incompressible flows and porous media flows through the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman interface conditions. A fully discrete numerical scheme has been proposed and analyzed employing backward Euler temporal discretization and a locally conservative LDG scheme for the space discretization. The well-posedness of the numerical scheme has been obtained under a small data condition. Optimal a priori error estimates have been proven in the energy norm, as well as the L2-norm for t>0. Numerical experiments ensure the efficiency of the theoretical results

entries.name: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
entries.abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

entries.name: Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem
entries.abstract: For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton. Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.

entries.name: A Unified View of Operator Splitting and Interior-Point Methods
entries.abstract: First-order splitting and interior-point methods offer contrasting computational trade-offs for convex conic quadratic programs, yet their linear systems look remarkably similar. We make this connection precise through the Moreau slack, an unconstrained variable from which multipliers and (ordinary) slacks satisfying exact or barrier-perturbed complementarity are recovered. The remaining feasibility equations define a unified residual whose roots are KKT points at zero barrier parameter and central-path points at positive barrier parameter. Applying splitting to this residual yields projection methods at zero barrier parameter and barrier splitting at positive parameter; Newton's method in the latter setting gives an implicit interior-point method. At fixed positive barrier parameter, matching the splitting metric to current barrier curvature equalises the primal variable corrections under the same regularisation and leaves a factor of two between the Moreau-slack corrections. With metrics frozen at a barrier solution, local analysis identifies when doubling improves (local) convergence and when the primal solve remains the bottleneck. Metric choices that simplify linear solves (eg make them diagonal) become Newton regularisations, exposing a shared convergence cost associated with computational convenience. Finally, a computable defect in the regularised Newton equations gives an accuracy-based criterion for reusing a splitting factorisation.

entries.name: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
entries.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^γy,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $γ\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a Bôcher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincaré condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\logρ$ term, $ρ=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $ρ^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.

entries.name: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
entries.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

entries.name: Quantales Arising From Rings
entries.abstract: We study the quantale, or multiplicative lattice, of additive submonoids of an arbitrary ring, with particular focus on the question of which properties of the ring can be recovered from it. We show that this quantale, unlike the better-known quantale of ideals, captures significant information about the cardinality, characteristic, and center of the ring. Certain rings, such as non-prime finite fields, torsion-free rings, and those with characteristic 2, are completely determined by their submonoid quantales. We also discuss various other subobject quantales one can associate to a (semi)ring.

entries.name: Holomorphic Foliations with a Single Singularity on Orbifold Projective Surfaces
entries.abstract: We investigate holomorphic foliations on orbifold projective surfaces with cyclic divisor class group, assuming that the foliation has a unique singular point of algebraic multiplicity one. If the normal degree of the foliation is sufficiently large, then we prove that it admits no invariant algebraic curve. Furthermore, we present several examples showing that the bound obtained is optimal.

entries.name: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
entries.abstract: We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $ζ_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $ζ_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.

entries.name: Uniqueness and comparison for a singular parabolic equation with a concave nonlinearity
entries.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for $\partial_t u-Δu=|x|^{-γ}u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, with $0<q<1$, $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$ and nonnegative initial data $u_0\in C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $s\mapsto s^q$ is not Lipschitz continuous at the origin, the uniqueness of nonnegative solutions is a delicate issue. {For $u_0\not\equiv0$, it was known for small values of $γ$ and, more recently, under the additional condition $γ<N(1-q)$.} We prove that, for $u_0\not\equiv0$, uniqueness holds on the whole range $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$, which settles a conjecture of the authors. In fact, we establish a comparison principle between bounded subsolutions and supersolutions which are bounded from below by a multiple of the profile $t^{1/(1-q)}(|x|+\sqrt t\,)^{-γ/(1-q)}$. We then describe completely the set of nonnegative solutions emanating from $u_0\equiv0$: it consists of the trivial solution, of a unique positive solution $U$, and of the delayed copies $U(\cdot,(t-τ)_+)$, $τ>0$. The solution $U$ is radially symmetric and self-similar, it obeys {two-sided pointwise bounds by multiples of the same profile}, and it is the limit of the solutions with nontrivial data as the data decrease to zero. Finally, we show that $U$ describes the large-time behavior of every nontrivial solution. The proofs replace the singular Gronwall inequality used in earlier work by a quotient estimate which exploits the concavity of $s\mapsto s^q$ and requires no smallness condition.

entries.name: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
entries.abstract: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $ω(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an étale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

entries.name: A Characterization of Tangle Matroids
entries.abstract: We prove that a matroid with at least two elements is a tangle matroid if and only if it cannot be covered by three hyperplanes. Some consequences of this theorem are also noted. In particular, no binary matroid of rank at least two is a tangle matroid.

entries.name: Euler Characteristics of Perverse Sheaves on Complex Ball Quotients
entries.abstract: Let $X=Γ\backslash\mathbb{B}^n$ be a finite-volume complex ball quotient with neat lattice. We prove that every nonzero algebraically constructible perverse sheaf on $X$ has positive Euler characteristic. More generally, we establish a criterion for strict positivity on smooth quasi-projective varieties whose logarithmic cotangent bundle is nef and admits an ample negative rational twist of the boundary divisor. For perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support, we give a lower bound in terms of the intrinsic geometry of $X$ for both proper and nonproper quotients. The bound depends on the systole of $X$ and tends to infinity with it. In particular, the minimum Euler characteristic among perverse sheaves with positive-dimensional support tends to infinity as one passes to higher levels of any cofinal normal tower of finite covers. We also deduce lower bounds for the middle intersection Betti numbers of projective subvarieties and boundedness of supports with bounded middle intersection cohomology.

entries.name: A strict Neumann-Dirichlet eigenvalue inequality on planar domains
entries.abstract: On simply connected, bounded planar Lipschitz domains it is known from our earlier work that the ($k+2$)-nd eigenvalue of the Neumann Laplacian cannot exceed the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. In this note we sharpen this statement by showing that this inequality is always strict. This was previously only known under additional assumptions.

entries.name: Common tiles from fractional tiles for two lattices
entries.abstract: Let $L_1, L_2\subseteq{\mathbb R}^d$ be lattices of the same volume and let $D_1, D_2$ be two bounded fundamental domains for $L_1, L_2$. We show that there is a measurable common tile for $L_1$ and $L_2$ contained in $D_1+D_2$. The main tool is a result of Bowen, Kun and Sabok (2021) which shows how to obtain a measurable perfect matching given a fractional perfect matching in hyperfinite graphings.

entries.name: $C^*(\mathbb{F}_2\times\mathbb{F}_2)$ fails the local lifting property
entries.abstract: We prove that the full group \(C^*\)-algebra \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) fails the local lifting property for all integers \(k,m\ge2\), and therefore disprove Ozawa's Strong Kirchberg Conjecture. Our proof is inspired by a construction of Ioana concerning Hilbert--Schmidt stability. We then strengthen this result by showing that \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) does not locally embed into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\). Consequently, the lifting property, the local lifting property, and local embeddability into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\) are not preserved under maximal tensor products.

entries.name: Standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart rings have unimodal $h$-vectors
entries.abstract: We prove that the $h$-vector $(h_0,\ldots,h_s)$ of every standard graded nearly Gorenstein Ehrhart ring is unimodal, with a peak at position $\lceil s/2\rceil$. More generally, a standard graded Ehrhart ring has an alternatingly increasing $h$-vector if the radical of the ideal generated by the degree-one part of its canonical trace ideal contains the homogeneous maximal ideal. In characteristic zero or two, the generic Artinian reduction of each such ring has the strong Lefschetz property. We also prove unimodality for every standard graded nearly Gorenstein domain of dimension at least two with $h$-vector $(1,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$, where $s\geq2$, provided that $h_1-h_s\leq1$. In the level case this $h$-vector is both concave and alternatingly increasing. If $h_1=h_s$, then $h_1=\cdots=h_s$.

entries.name: A remark on cohomological and Chow decompositions of the diagonal
entries.abstract: We construct a quartic double solid whose desingularization admits an integral cohomological decomposition of the diagonal but no Chow decomposition.

entries.name: Modularity of Heegner Cycles and Arithmetic Inner Products on Kuga-Sato Varieties
entries.abstract: For \(κ\ge2\), the principal part of a weakly holomorphic modular form of weight \(\tfrac32-κ\) determines a linear combination of codimension-\(κ\) Heegner cycles on a compact Kuga--Sato variety. We use isogeny correspondences to prove that every such combination vanishes in the Chow group with complex coefficients. These rational equivalences imply that the generating series of Heegner cycles is a Chow-valued cusp form of weight \(κ+\tfrac12\) at every level and for every compatible fundamental twist. We prove an arithmetic inner product formula for theta lifts on the modular curve \(X_0(N)\) and on higher-dimensional Kuga--Sato varieties. It expresses their height pairings in terms of central derivatives of quadratic twists of newform \(L\)-functions, with an explicit product of local operators on oldspaces. On each primitive newform line selected by the twist, the height of one projected Heegner cycle at a fundamental index with nonzero Fourier coefficient determines all pairings of projected cycles on that line. This specialization recovers the Gross--Zagier formula in weight two and the genus-character case of the Gross--Zagier--Zhang formula in higher weight.

entries.name: Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions
entries.abstract: We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli (2013); a proof of polynomial mixing remained one of the major challenges in the field. We prove this polynomial mixing time bound at all low temperatures. The key step is to establish fast mixing of the interface separating the plus and minus phases on a box with Dobrushin boundary conditions. In simpler models of height functions, polynomial bounds tend to rely on exact harmonic properties and connections to a discrete heat equation. However, the Ising interface exhibits microscopic defects that necessitate the development of a more robust method. We address this via a new multiscale approach to bound mixing times of general disordered random-walk bridges that homogenize to a Brownian bridge at mesoscopic scales. Another notable ingredient is a novel application of censoring to reduce the mixing time problem to proving only a weak Poincaré inequality, or warm-start mixing bound, allowing us to assume suitable regularity conditions on the interface and bubbles.

entries.name: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees
entries.abstract: We study the Bergman projection $P_ω$ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_ω$, where $ω$ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_ω$ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $A^p_ω$ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $ω$ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_ω^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(ω) $ to $L^p(ω) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $Ω\in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(Ω) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_Ω(\mathbb{D}) $.

entries.name: On the space of left orders on the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H \text{ and }G_\infty$
entries.abstract: We introduce the notion of a left order on a group with a certain specification of signs for the elements of a subset. We obtain an equivalent criterion for the existence of such a left order and apply it to obtain a new proof of the fact that any of the groups $QI(\mathbb{R}_+),\,QI(\mathbb{R}_+)/H,\,G_\infty$ admits infinitely many non-Conradian left orders. We introduce the notion of separation of free subsemigroups of a left ordered group by its left translation induced actions on a point in the group and show that the above three groups admit such left orders. We also construct a subset of the set of left orders on any of the three groups, show the subset is a perfect set and give a new proof of the fact that the sets of the left orders on these three groups are uncountable.

entries.name: Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm
entries.abstract: We study Cop-Win Edge Completion: given a graph $G$, find the minimum number $\copfill(G)$ of edges whose addition lets one cop capture a visible robber. We first give an exact reduction from Dominating Set, constructing for every nonempty graph $H$ a graph $G_H$ on $2|V(H)|+2$ vertices with $\copfill(G_H)=γ(H)$. This resolves a complexity question of Mertzios et al. and implies NP-completeness even for connected graphs of diameter two with a dominating edge and domination number two. Interestingly, while Minimum Fill-in is fixed-parameter tractable in the number $k$ of added edges, Cop-Win Edge Completion, whose target class strictly contains the connected chordal graphs, is W[2]-hard parameterized by $k$, even by $k+γ(G)$. We then give two lower bounds. The first, $\copfill(G)\ge 2n-m-b-c-1$, where $n,m,b,c$ count vertices, edges, nontrivial blocks, and components, is tight for partial 2-trees, giving a linear-time algorithm for the optimum value and a quadratic-time construction; for outerplanar graphs, an optimum completion preserving outerplanarity is found in linear time. The second, based on the cycle space modulo the subspace generated by triangles, gives $\copfill(G)=c-1+\sum_{i=1}^r(\ell_i-3)$ for block-cactus graphs with long cycle blocks of lengths $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r$. We also show how the optimum behaves under disjoint unions and joins, yielding a polynomial-time algorithm for $P_4$-sparse graphs, including cographs, and exact formulas for complete multipartite graphs. In contrast to partial 2-trees and block-cactus graphs, an optimum cop-win completion can be much smaller than a minimum chordal one, already on complete bipartite graphs. Finally, we give FPT algorithms for $k+\mathrm{nd}(G)$, for the twin-cover number $t$ alone in time $2^{O(t^3)}n^{O(1)}$, and for $k+\mathrm{tw}(G)$.

entries.name: Self-similar solutions for capillary water waves
entries.abstract: In this paper we prove the existence of self-similar solutions to the capillary water wave problem. In particular, this implies finite-time formation of singularities in the form of a corner, and retraction from a corner due to the time-reversibility of the equations. Unlike most self-similar smooth solutions, the solutions with $2/3$ time-length scaling are seen in experiments like pinch-off retraction, bubble bursting or jet formation. The proof involves a new argument through the regularization of the Hamiltonian and does not require the existence of an approximate profile. We believe this strategy has further implications in the construction of self-similar solutions of dispersive PDE.

entries.name: Toward a Classification of Differentially $3$-Uniform Power Mappings over $\F_{p^2}$ and $\F_{p^3}$
entries.abstract: We study the classification, up to the CCZ-equivalence, of differentially $3$-uniform power mappings over quadratic and cubic extensions of prime fields. Over $\F_{p^2}$ exhaustive searches for primes $3<p<300$ found only the known families E1 and E4 for $p>23$. Over $\F_{p^3}$, the previously unexplained exponents for $7<p<200$ belong to a single family. We give an elementary proof that this family has differential uniformity at most $3$ for primes $p\equiv 3 \pmod 4$, and prove that the bound is attained for $p>1444$.

entries.name: Matching Under Metric Privacy
entries.abstract: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $Θ\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. Benchmark experiments support $d\approx\log n$ as a practical guide to the transition between directly randomizing point coordinates and using Gumbel matching. Extensions to squared Euclidean costs enable private nonparametric two-sample hypothesis testing. These results show how the application's trust model guides representation and dimension choices for better utility: under local privacy, low-dimensional point representations reduce excess cost, while under central privacy, distance representations achieve the optimal rate even in high dimension.

entries.name: Double-dimer loops in the biased Aztec diamond converge to a diffeomorphic image of nested $CLE_4$
entries.abstract: We superimpose two independent domino tilings of the Aztec diamond of order $N$, with vertical weight $a>0$ and horizontal weight $1$. Represent each domino by the edge joining the centers of its two squares. The edges used by exactly one tiling form loops. After rescaling by $N^{-1}$, the full loop collection converges in law to the image of the nested conformal loop ensemble $\CLE_4$ under the diffeomorphism \[ w\longmapsto \frac{2(\Re w+\ii a\,\Im w)}{\sqrt{1+a^2}\,(1+|w|^2)} \] from the unit disk onto the liquid region of the rescaled diamond. Thus the bias rescales the horizontal and vertical coordinates of the unbiased limit. The topology of convergence records loop multiplicities and the order of traversal around each loop, up to reversal. Transfer estimates in the Krawtchouk basis control slab traversals and opposite crossings along entire sections, including where they meet the arctic ellipse. These estimates give tightness and, together with finite-puncture observables, identify the limit and rule out backtracking.

entries.name: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
entries.abstract: Physics simulation outputs increasingly come from solvers that no expert inspects, such as third-party packages in automated pipelines, programs written by large language models (LLMs), and learned surrogates. In earlier work on cardiac pulsed field ablation, we proposed that solvers return a certificate with their answers. The certificate consists of an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current, and a small independent checker turns it into guaranteed error bounds against a written specification of the physics. Here, the same checker verifies the outputs of other solvers on the same problem. Specifically, FEniCSx computes both fields and receives the same bounds as our own solver. Five plausible bugs in a correct solver, one of them about 0.2% from the true impedance, all converge and pass a grid convergence study, yet the certificate rejects or refutes all five. Of three solvers written by LLMs, one is correct and certified to 0.1%, and one never solves the equation but converges. Neural networks that predict the coefficients of a reduced basis emit admissible fields and receive valid per-prediction bounds, at most 0.0021% wide inside their training range and 0.3-25% wide outside it, where 90% conformal intervals cover none of 14 tests. Untuned Fourier neural operators with free nodal outputs receive valid but uninformative bounds. On a uniform grid, interpolation onto the certificate grid limits them, and on the certificate grid, thin cells turn small nodal errors into large energy errors. Energy-norm training narrows the certified interval tenfold, and projecting the nodal-loss outputs onto the reduced basis narrows it by two to four orders of magnitude, still uninformative. The guarantee concerns the stated model and holds for any output, wherever its input lies. It is informative only when the output is accurate in energy on a grid that resolves the problem.

entries.name: Diophantine sets over global function fields
entries.abstract: Let $q\equiv 3\bmod 4$ be a prime power and let $K$ be a finite separable extension of the field of rational functions $\mathbb F_q(t)$, with constant field $\mathbb F_q$. We show that $\mathbb F_q[t]$ is Diophantine in $\mathbb F_q(t)$ and that the latter is Diophantine in $K$. We deduce from work of Demeyer that $K$ has the DPRM property: Diophantine sets over $K$ are the same as listable sets.

entries.name: Upper bound $2^{n}-1$ for chromatic number of orbit polytope of a small cover is attained for every $n\geq4$
entries.abstract: Davis and Januszkiewicz proved that the facets of a simple $n$-polytope $P$ which is the orbit space of a small cover can be properly coloured by $2^{n}-1$ colours. The bound is sharp for $n=2$, it is not sharp for $n=3$ by the Four Color Theorem, and it was shown to be sharp for $n=4$ by the first author. We show that it is sharp for every $n\geq4$. The polytope is obtained from the dual of the cyclic polytope $C^{n}(2^{n}-1)$ by truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$. The resolution works over an arbitrary field and gives the sharp bound $(q^{n}-1)/(q-1)$ over the field with $q$ elements. More generally, every simple $n$-polytope whose facets can be properly coloured by $k\leq2^{n}-1$ colours becomes, after truncations of faces of codimension at least $3$, the orbit polytope of a small cover with the same chromatic number $k$. We also construct, for every $n\geq4$, a simple $n$-polytope with $χ=2^{n}-1$ which is the orbit space of both a small cover and a quasitoric manifold, and in the oriented case we obtain the sharp bound $2^{n-1}$ for every $n\geq4$.

entries.name: On the linearization of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation in $\mathbb{R}^N$
entries.abstract: Let $u$ be a positive radial solution of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation $$-Δu=u^p \qquad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad p>\frac{N+2}{N-2}. $$ In this paper we classify the bounded solutions of the associated linearized operator $-Δw -pu^{p-1}w=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The resulting classification reveals the role of the threshold value $p=\frac{N + \sqrt{N^2 - 8N}}{4}$. In particular, above this threshold, the solutions are generated by the invariance of the problem under dilations and translations. Below this threshold, many new solutions appear, and their number tends to infinity as $p$ approaches the Joseph-Lundgren exponent and $N$ is large.

entries.name: A proof of the chemical recurrence conjecture in two dimensions
entries.abstract: At the microscopic level, the dynamics of a network of chemical reactions can be modeled, in the well-mixed case, as a continuous-time Markov chain. This process counts the number of particles in each of the $d$ species as a function of time, and its state-dependent, polynomial jump rates are determined by the structure of the underlying reaction graph. Networks of chemical reactions whose reaction graphs are the union of strongly connected components are called \emph{weakly reversible}. The long-standing \emph{chemical recurrence conjecture} states that if a network is weakly reversible, then the associated Markov chain is positive recurrent. We prove this conjecture for $d=2$.

entries.name: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
entries.abstract: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.

entries.name: Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I
entries.abstract: We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-π^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$. We prove a central limit theorem for the Green energy by combining local Bergman kernel asymptotics with an expansion for the cumulants. A central limit theorem also holds for the logarithmic energy of Bergman determinantal point process on complex manifolds.

entries.name: A Boundary Comparison Method for Gaussian Fluctuations in Planar Euclidean Optimization
entries.abstract: We develop a boundary comparison method for Gaussian fluctuations of optimization costs on planar random points, including traveling-salesman length, minimum perfect-matching length, and the Held--Karp relaxation. A local change can alter an optimal solution far from the modified points, making a direct decomposition into local contributions difficult. Our criterion requires the difference between the changes in the full and local costs caused by the same replacement to be controlled at the boundary scale, allowing a smaller-order $L^2$ excess. Under this condition, the centered difference between the total cost and the sum of independent cell costs vanishes in $L^2$. The multiscale argument shows that a nonvanishing variance of the cutting error would produce Gaussian tails incompatible with the boundary control. We obtain joint Gaussian limits for the three centered costs, using a conditional version for matching, and prove that the limiting covariance is positive definite in the Euclidean case. Convergence holds in quadratic Wasserstein distance for Poisson and fixed sample sizes. The results extend jointly to finitely many planar norms and to fixed sampling laws whose absolutely continuous component has a density positive almost everywhere on the square, with an arbitrary singular component.

entries.name: On Prime Values of Bunyakovsky's Polynomials and Prime Products of Schinzel's Polynomials
entries.abstract: First, we prove a theorem of the number of primes in short intervals with a much more accurate estimation of prime numbers, the error range of which is less than $x^{1/2-0.0327283}$ for $x\geq10^{41}$. The theorem states as follows: Given a positive real number $β$ that determines a real number $x_β$ by $e(\log x_β)^{3}/x_β^{0.0327283}=β$, let $Φ(x):=βx^{1/2}$ for $x\geq x_β$ where $Φ(x):=x^{1/2}$ when let $β=1$. Then there are \[ \frac{π(x+Φ(x))-π(x)}{Φ(x)/\log x}=1+O(\frac{1}{\log x}) \] and \[ \lim_{x \to \infty}\frac{π(x+Φ(x))-π(x)}{Φ(x)/\log x}=1. \] Next, based on the theorem, Bunyakovsky's polynomials, Schinzel's polynomials, and Schinzel's polynomials with a negative leading coefficient are researched. Results show that (1) given a Bunyakovsky's polynomial $f(x)$, $f(m)$ is prime for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (2) given a Schinzel's polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}f_{i}(x)$, all numbers $f_{1}(m)$, $f_{2}(m)$, $\ldots$, $f_{k}(m)$ are primes for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (3) given a Schinzel's polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}f_{i}(x)$ with a negative leading coefficient for $f_{k}(x)$ and positive leading coefficients for others, all numbers $f_{1}(m)$, $f_{2}(m)$, $\ldots$, $f_{k}(m)$ are primes for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (4) so some other conjectures in the number theory are proved.

entries.name: On a Conjecture About the Sombor Index of Graphs
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. A graph invariant for $G$ is a number related to the structure of $G$ which is invariant under the symmetry of $G$}. The Sombor and reduced Sombor indices of $G$ are two new graph invariants defined as $SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2}$ and $SO_{red}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{\big(d_G(u)-1\big)^2 + \big(d_G(v)-1\big)^2}$, respectively, where $d_G(v)$ is the degree of the vertex $v$ in $G$. We denote by $H_{n,ν}$ the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $ν$ edge(s), $0\leq ν\leq n-2$, between a fixed pendent vertex and $ν$ other pendent vertices. Réti et al. [T. Réti, T Došlić and A. Ali, On the Sombor index of graphs, \textit{Contrib. Math.} \textbf{3} (2021) 11--18] proposed a conjecture that the graph $H_{n,ν}$ has the maximum Sombor index among all connected $ν$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, where $0\leq\,ν\leq n-2$. In some earlier works the validity of this conjecture was proved for $ν\leq 5$. In this paper we confirm that this conjecture is true, when $ν= 6$. The Sombor index in the case that the number of pendent vertices is less than or equal to $n - ν- 2$ is investigated and the same results are obtained for the reduced Sombor index. Some relationships between Sombor, reduced Sombor and first Zagreb indices of graphs are also obtained.

entries.name: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
entries.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

entries.name: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
entries.abstract: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

entries.name: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
entries.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

entries.name: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
entries.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

entries.name: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
entries.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

entries.name: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
entries.abstract: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.

entries.name: Degenerate symplectic fixed points and Gromov-Witten invariants
entries.abstract: We establish a connection between Gromov--Witten invariants and the number of fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed rational symplectic manifolds, without assuming nondegeneracy, via deformed Hamiltonian spectral invariants. We obtain a Hamiltonian fixed point estimate involving Gromov--Witten invariants with one point insertion under an explicit minimum-area hypothesis. We propose three conjectures about Hamiltonian fixed point estimate and prove them for every generalized flag manifold $X=G/P$ equipped with a rational Kähler form. We extend Schwarz's quantum cuplength to deformed quantum cuplength for symplectic periods and use it to obtain estimates on monotone symplectic manifolds admitting nonzero mixed Gromov--Witten invariants. We use the quantum-factorization estimate to recover the Fano toric case of Givental's symplectic fixed-point theorem. Finally, a graded spectral-carrier argument gives uniform fixed-point bounds on negatively monotone manifolds.

entries.name: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
entries.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.

entries.name: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
entries.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

entries.name: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
entries.abstract: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.

entries.name: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
entries.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

entries.name: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
entries.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

entries.name: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
entries.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehatΞ_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehatΞ_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite étale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $μ_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.

entries.name: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
entries.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

entries.name: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
entries.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

entries.name: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
entries.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

entries.name: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
entries.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces.
