A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

entries.name: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
entries.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

entries.name: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
entries.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

entries.name: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
entries.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

entries.name: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
entries.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

entries.name: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
entries.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

entries.name: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers -- A simple Introduction
entries.abstract: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. We give an elementary introduction to the subject.

entries.name: OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture: A harmonic analytic perspective
entries.abstract: This note presents OpenAI's proof of the local smoothing conjecture. It is written for harmonic analysts who may be new to quaternionic Monge--Ampère equations. We introduce the quaternionic Hessian and explain how the associated determinant equation leads to the critical annular estimate.

entries.name: No coexistence in the two-type Richardson model when one side is stronger than the other
entries.abstract: We study the two-type Richardson model in two dimensions. We prove that there is no coexistence of the two species when their infection rates are different, establishing a conjecture of H{ä}ggstr{ö}m and Pemantle from 1997. In our proof we analyze a second order approximation of the infected region and use a Mermin--Wagner style argument to push the strong type out of the weak one.

entries.name: Signed Admissible Regions and 2-adic Area Obstructions for Perfect Triangles
entries.abstract: A perfect triangle is a triangle whose sides, medians and area are all integers; whether one exists is an open problem. We study Buchholz's rational parametrization of triangles with two rational medians on the whole $(θ,φ)$-plane, allowing the generated side lengths to be negative. We factor its Heron polynomial $H(θ,φ)$ into ten explicit factors and show that the points whose componentwise absolute values form a triangle are exactly those with $H>0$; the points giving positive side lengths directly form three open quadrilaterals, one of which is the region used by Buchholz and Rathbun. Every triangle with two rational medians arises from sixteen signed parameter points, given by explicit rational functions. Rational area forces $H$ to be a square in $\mathbb{Q}_2$, and the valuation and the unit part of $H$ yield parity and modulo-8 conditions in three valuation ranges. Since a triangle is excluded as soon as one of its sixteen parameter points fails a test, these conditions exclude infinite families of signed admissible parameters, including non-integral ones. The conditions are necessary only and do not settle the existence of perfect triangles.

entries.name: Generic Strong Regularity and the Branson--Gover Conjecture
entries.abstract: On each closed smooth manifold of even dimension $2N\ge 4$, we prove that the Branson--Gover detour operators are strongly regular in every degree $k-1$, $1\le k<N$, on a $C^\infty$-open dense set of Riemannian metrics. Consequently, every de Rham cohomology class of positive degree below the middle dimension has a unique conformal harmonic representative for these metrics. On a connected manifold, the critical scalar GJMS operator has only constants in its kernel on an open dense set of conformal structures modulo diffeomorphisms isotopic to the identity, as conjectured by Canzani, Gover, Jakobson, and Ponge. The proof computes the principal symbol of a reduced metric Hessian that accounts for the motion of the kernel through a Green operator.

entries.name: A one-third bound for domination in cubic graphs of girth at least six
entries.abstract: A set $S\subseteq V(G)$ is a dominating set of a graph $G$ if every vertex outside $S$ has a neighbor in $S$. The domination number $γ(G)$ is the minimum size of a dominating set of $G$. In 2010, Verstraëte conjectured that every cubic graph $G$ of order $n$ and girth at least six satisfies $γ(G)\le n/3$. More recently, Dorbec and Henning established this bound under the additional assumption that $G$ contains neither a $7$-cycle nor an $8$-cycle. We prove Verstraëte's conjecture in full. As a corollary, we settle the $C_4$-free case of Kostochka's conjecture, which asserts that the same bound holds for all cubic bipartite graphs.

entries.name: A sharp threshold in the Li--Lin open problem
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study positive solutions to the problem \begin{equation*} -Δu = |x|^{-s_2}u^{2^*(s_2)-1} - \la |x|^{-s_1}u^{p-1} \quad \text{in }\Om, \qquad u=0 \quad \text{on }\partial\Om, \end{equation*} where $\Om\subset\R^N$ ($N\ge 3$) is a bounded domain with $0\in\partial\Om$, $0\le s_1<s_2<2$, $2^*(s)=\frac{2(N-s)}{N-2}$, $2^*(s_2)<p<2^*(s_1)$, and $\la>0$. This is the Li--Lin open problem \cite{LL} in the form studied by Cerami, Zhong, and Zou \cite{CZZ} and by Tang and Tang \cite{TT1}. Assume that $\partial\Om$ is $C^{1,α}$ near $0$ with a leading term of homogeneity $1+α$, and set $θ=\frac{(N-2)(2^*(s_1)-p)}{2}$. We prove that a solution exists for every $\la>0$ if $θ>α$ and the $α$-mean curvature of $\partial\Om$ at $0$ is negative, whereas $\la^*=\sup\{\la>0:\text{a solution exists}\}$ is finite if $θ\leα$, without any curvature assumption. For $α=1$, this removes the restriction to almost every $\la$ in \cite[Theorem 1.6]{CZZ}, answers a question of Zou \cite{Z}, and disproves the conjecture in \cite[Remark 1.7]{TT1}. The proofs rely on a scale-invariant estimate uniform in $\la$, a Hadamard-type identity for the half-space extremal and a localized Pohozaev identity combined with sharp decay estimates. Notably, no regularity of $\partial\Om$ is required away from $0$.

entries.name: Connected descent and Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles
entries.abstract: We answer a question by Hui Zhang and show that, for any smooth, quasi-projective, geometrically integral variety X over a number field k, the connected descent set for 0-cycles is equal to the Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. In particular, the connected descent and the abelianised connected descent sets for 0-cycles coincide. In the same spirit, we also show that the descent set under all tori for 0-cycles is equal to the algebraic Brauer-Manin set for 0-cycles. Finally, we give a new formulation of Conjecture (E) using the connected descent sets.

entries.name: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
entries.abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.

entries.name: On the quaternionic Goldberg conjecture
entries.abstract: We prove a quaternionic Kähler analogue of the Goldberg conjecture, namely: Let $(M^8,g,Ω)$ denote a compact $8$-manifold endowed with an $\mathrm{Sp}(2)\mathrm{Sp}(1)$-structure defined by a closed $4$-form $Ω$. If the metric $g$ is Einstein with non-negative scalar curvature then it is quaternionic Kähler i.e. $Ω$ is parallel. In fact we prove a slightly stronger result allowing for the scalar curvature to be negative under a suitable pinching condition by the square norm of the intrinsic torsion.

entries.name: On the work of Jacob Tsimerman
entries.abstract: Jacob Tsimerman was awarded a Fields Medal at the\ ICM in Philadelphia on July 23, 2026 ``For his contribution in the recasting of o-minimality as a fundamental method of arithmetic and complex algebraic geometry, and his role in the proof of many central conjectures including Griffiths' conjecture on the algebraicity of images of the period maps, and the André-Oort conjecture for Siegel modular varieties.'' We describe this work.

entries.name: Positivity and multivariate extensions of two-parameter Askey-Wilson moments
entries.abstract: Kim and Stanton showed that certain specialized Askey--Wilson moments are polynomials with integer coefficients after normalization, and conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative. We refine this into the conjecture for the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments and prove the refinement by establishing a manifestly positive recurrence. We also construct a combinatorial model that expresses the normalized Askey--Wilson mixed moments as weighted sums of decorated partial matchings. This model specializes to the partial matching model for the mixed moments of continuous $q$-Hermite polynomials. Finally, we consider the corresponding multivariate moments and prove that their minimal numerators have nonnegative coefficients up to an explicit sign.

entries.name: Normalized Weyl Energy and the Differential Topology of Four-Manifolds
entries.abstract: The Weyl functional $\int_M\|W_g\|^2\,dμ_g$ plays an important role in four dimensional conformal geometry. Using this functional, Chang, Gursky, and Zhang introduced an invariant of an admissible conformal class and a smooth invariant of the underlying manifold obtained by taking the infimum over all such classes. We use a normalization in which both invariants, denoted by $β(M,c)$ and $β(M)$, take values in $[0,1)$. We prove that every admissible four-manifold $M$ with $β(M)$ sufficiently close to $1/2$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ up to reversal of orientation. At $β(M)=1/2$, this result and the conformal characterization of the Fubini--Study class confirm Conjecture~1.1 of Chang, Gursky, and Zhang. Among admissible four-manifolds with indefinite intersection form, we prove the corresponding stability of the diffeomorphism type of $S^2\times S^2$ near $2/3$. For the one- and two-point blow-ups of $\mathbb{CP}^2$, we show that $β(M)$ lies strictly above the respective topological lower bounds of $2/3$ and $23/30$. These results lead us to ask whether $1$ is the only accumulation point of the values of $β(M)$ and whether, among simply connected admissible four-manifolds, $β(M)$ determines the diffeomorphism type up to reversal of orientation.

entries.name: Monsky's nodal cubic and the arithmetic of Frobenius invariants
entries.abstract: We prove Monsky's conjecture on the colengths of the ideals $(x^q,y^q,z^q,h^j)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2[x,y,z]$, where $h=x^3+y^3+xyz$, $q=2^e$, and $0\le j\le q$. We derive Monsky's recursion by interchanging the values of sections of syzygy bundles on the two branches at the node of the cubic $h=0$. For the hypersurface $uv+h=0$, the Hilbert-Kunz and Frobenius splitting series are algebraic of degree two over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. For $uv+h(X_1)+\cdots+h(X_m)=0$, where the $X_i$ are disjoint triples of variables and $m\ge 2$, both series are transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}(w)$. When $m=2$, we express the Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity in terms of a period of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero. This gives an explicit seven-dimensional hypersurface over $\mathbb{F}_2$ with transcendental Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity and transcendental $F$-signature.

entries.name: A martingale proof of simultaneous convex and smooth renorming
entries.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to Problem 198 of Guirao, Montesinos, and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~90], also formulated by Pisier [\emph{Martingales in Banach Spaces}, Cambridge University Press (2016), p.~461]. Given equivalent norms with convexity of power type $p$ and smoothness of power type $q$, respectively, we construct a single equivalent norm with both properties using finite dyadic martingales. It can be chosen arbitrarily close to the given smooth norm in multiplicative distortion and preserves all linear symmetries shared by the two initial norms. The case $p=q=2$ with group invariance answers Problem 3.6 of Cabello Sánchez, Ferenczi, and Randrianantoanina [São Paulo J. Math. Sci. \textbf{16} (2022), 406--458].

entries.name: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
entries.abstract: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $λ> 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $λ> 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

entries.name: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
entries.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

entries.name: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
entries.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

entries.name: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
entries.abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.

entries.name: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
entries.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

entries.name: The optimal exponent in the Erdős--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums
entries.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.

entries.name: Unified Schur multiple zeta functions
entries.abstract: We define symmetric multiple zeta values, unified zeta functions, and finite zeta values in the Schur setting. We establish a Jacobi--Trudi formula and a Giambelli formula for unified Schur multiple zeta functions, and we show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between finite and symmetric Schur multiple zeta values under the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture. We also show a vanishing property for a symmetric sum of finite Schur multiple zeta values, generalizing a result obtained by Hoffman for finite multiple zeta values.

entries.name: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
entries.abstract: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.

entries.name: Sharpness of the Brjuno Condition for Hyperbolic Bishop Surfaces
entries.abstract: Let $μ\in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|μ|=1$, and assume that $μ$ is not a root of unity and is not Brjuno. Let $Q_γ$ denote the Bishop quadric with $γ= 1/\sqrt{2+μ+μ^{-1}} > 1/2$. Gong and Stolovitch conjectured that there exists a real-analytic surface in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with Moser--Webster invariant $μ$ that is formally but not holomorphically equivalent to $Q_γ$. We prove this conjecture.

entries.name: Gaudin's determinantal norm formula and Hall--Littlewood polynomials
entries.abstract: The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

entries.name: The monodromy conjecture for remarkable poles
entries.abstract: We prove the strong monodromy conjecture for the remarkable numbers of a regular function f on a smooth complex variety. We show more generally that the log canonical modification of f computes the remarkable numbers and gives roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of f.

entries.name: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
entries.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

entries.name: Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space
entries.abstract: We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by Pérez, Rodríguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(κ,τ)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $τ$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.

entries.name: Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points
entries.abstract: In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.

entries.name: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
entries.abstract: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.

entries.name: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
entries.abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

entries.name: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
entries.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

entries.name: Uniqueness and comparison for a singular parabolic equation with a concave nonlinearity
entries.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for $\partial_t u-Δu=|x|^{-γ}u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, with $0<q<1$, $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$ and nonnegative initial data $u_0\in C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $s\mapsto s^q$ is not Lipschitz continuous at the origin, the uniqueness of nonnegative solutions is a delicate issue. {For $u_0\not\equiv0$, it was known for small values of $γ$ and, more recently, under the additional condition $γ<N(1-q)$.} We prove that, for $u_0\not\equiv0$, uniqueness holds on the whole range $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$, which settles a conjecture of the authors. In fact, we establish a comparison principle between bounded subsolutions and supersolutions which are bounded from below by a multiple of the profile $t^{1/(1-q)}(|x|+\sqrt t\,)^{-γ/(1-q)}$. We then describe completely the set of nonnegative solutions emanating from $u_0\equiv0$: it consists of the trivial solution, of a unique positive solution $U$, and of the delayed copies $U(\cdot,(t-τ)_+)$, $τ>0$. The solution $U$ is radially symmetric and self-similar, it obeys {two-sided pointwise bounds by multiples of the same profile}, and it is the limit of the solutions with nontrivial data as the data decrease to zero. Finally, we show that $U$ describes the large-time behavior of every nontrivial solution. The proofs replace the singular Gronwall inequality used in earlier work by a quotient estimate which exploits the concavity of $s\mapsto s^q$ and requires no smallness condition.

entries.name: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
entries.abstract: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $ω(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an étale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

entries.name: $C^*(\mathbb{F}_2\times\mathbb{F}_2)$ fails the local lifting property
entries.abstract: We prove that the full group \(C^*\)-algebra \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) fails the local lifting property for all integers \(k,m\ge2\), and therefore disprove Ozawa's Strong Kirchberg Conjecture. Our proof is inspired by a construction of Ioana concerning Hilbert--Schmidt stability. We then strengthen this result by showing that \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) does not locally embed into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\). Consequently, the lifting property, the local lifting property, and local embeddability into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\) are not preserved under maximal tensor products.

entries.name: A proof of the chemical recurrence conjecture in two dimensions
entries.abstract: At the microscopic level, the dynamics of a network of chemical reactions can be modeled, in the well-mixed case, as a continuous-time Markov chain. This process counts the number of particles in each of the $d$ species as a function of time, and its state-dependent, polynomial jump rates are determined by the structure of the underlying reaction graph. Networks of chemical reactions whose reaction graphs are the union of strongly connected components are called \emph{weakly reversible}. The long-standing \emph{chemical recurrence conjecture} states that if a network is weakly reversible, then the associated Markov chain is positive recurrent. We prove this conjecture for $d=2$.

papers.name: On Prime Values of Bunyakovsky's Polynomials and Prime Products of Schinzel's Polynomials
papers.abstract: First, we prove a theorem of the number of primes in short intervals with a much more accurate estimation of prime numbers, the error range of which is less than $x^{1/2-0.0327283}$ for $x\geq10^{41}$. The theorem states as follows: Given a positive real number $β$ that determines a real number $x_β$ by $e(\log x_β)^{3}/x_β^{0.0327283}=β$, let $Φ(x):=βx^{1/2}$ for $x\geq x_β$ where $Φ(x):=x^{1/2}$ when let $β=1$. Then there are \[ \frac{π(x+Φ(x))-π(x)}{Φ(x)/\log x}=1+O(\frac{1}{\log x}) \] and \[ \lim_{x \to \infty}\frac{π(x+Φ(x))-π(x)}{Φ(x)/\log x}=1. \] Next, based on the theorem, Bunyakovsky's polynomials, Schinzel's polynomials, and Schinzel's polynomials with a negative leading coefficient are researched. Results show that (1) given a Bunyakovsky's polynomial $f(x)$, $f(m)$ is prime for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (2) given a Schinzel's polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}f_{i}(x)$, all numbers $f_{1}(m)$, $f_{2}(m)$, $\ldots$, $f_{k}(m)$ are primes for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (3) given a Schinzel's polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}f_{i}(x)$ with a negative leading coefficient for $f_{k}(x)$ and positive leading coefficients for others, all numbers $f_{1}(m)$, $f_{2}(m)$, $\ldots$, $f_{k}(m)$ are primes for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (4) so some other conjectures in the number theory are proved.

papers.name: On a Conjecture About the Sombor Index of Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V(G)$ and edge set $E(G)$. A graph invariant for $G$ is a number related to the structure of $G$ which is invariant under the symmetry of $G$}. The Sombor and reduced Sombor indices of $G$ are two new graph invariants defined as $SO(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{d_G(u)^2 + d_G(v)^2}$ and $SO_{red}(G)=\sum_{uv\in E(G)}\sqrt{\big(d_G(u)-1\big)^2 + \big(d_G(v)-1\big)^2}$, respectively, where $d_G(v)$ is the degree of the vertex $v$ in $G$. We denote by $H_{n,ν}$ the graph constructed from the star $S_n$ by adding $ν$ edge(s), $0\leq ν\leq n-2$, between a fixed pendent vertex and $ν$ other pendent vertices. Réti et al. [T. Réti, T Došlić and A. Ali, On the Sombor index of graphs, \textit{Contrib. Math.} \textbf{3} (2021) 11--18] proposed a conjecture that the graph $H_{n,ν}$ has the maximum Sombor index among all connected $ν$-cyclic graphs of order $n$, where $0\leq\,ν\leq n-2$. In some earlier works the validity of this conjecture was proved for $ν\leq 5$. In this paper we confirm that this conjecture is true, when $ν= 6$. The Sombor index in the case that the number of pendent vertices is less than or equal to $n - ν- 2$ is investigated and the same results are obtained for the reduced Sombor index. Some relationships between Sombor, reduced Sombor and first Zagreb indices of graphs are also obtained.

papers.name: Regulators in the Arithmetic of Function Fields
papers.abstract: As a natural sequel to the study of A-motivic cohomology initiated in "On the integral part of A-motivic cohomology", we develop a notion of regulator for rigid analytically trivial Anderson A-motives. In accordance with the conjectural picture over number fields, we define it as the morphism at the level of extension modules induced by the exactness of the Hodge-Pink realization functor. The purpose of this article is twofold: first, we prove a finiteness result for A-motivic cohomology; second, under a weight assumption, we show that the source and the target of the regulator have the same dimension. It came as a surprise to the author that the image of this regulator may fail to have full rank, thereby preventing an analogue of Beilinson's celebrated conjecture from holding in our setting.

papers.name: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
papers.abstract: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

papers.name: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

papers.name: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
papers.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

papers.name: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
papers.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

papers.name: Three Theorems on Negami's Planar Cover Conjecture
papers.abstract: A long-standing Conjecture of S. Negami states that a connected graph has a finite planar cover if and only if it embeds in the projective plane. It is known that the Conjecture is equivalent to the fact that \emph{the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ has no finite planar cover}. We prove three theorems showing that the graph $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ admits no planar cover with certain structural properties, and that the minimal planar cover of $K_{1,2, 2, 2}$ (if it exists) must be $4$-connected.

papers.name: Scheduling in Queueing Systems with Uncertain and Evolving Holding Costs
papers.abstract: In queueing systems, the holding costs of jobs may evolve in uncertain ways. For example, in content moderation for social media platforms, the cost of delaying the review of a content piece is proportional to its view trajectory, which fluctuates and is a priori unknown. To capture such uncertain and evolving holding cost patterns, we consider a queueing model where job states evolve based on a Markov chain with state-dependent instantaneous holding costs. We demonstrate that in the presence of such uncertain and evolving holding costs, the two canonical algorithmic principles, instantaneous-cost ($cμ$-rule) and expected-remaining-cost ($cμ/θ$-rule), are suboptimal. By viewing each job as a Markovian ski-rental problem, we develop a new index-based algorithm, Opportunity-adjusted Remaining Cost (OaRC), that adjusts to the opportunity of serving jobs in the future when uncertainty partly resolves. We show that the suboptimality gap of OaRC scales as $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{N})$, where $N$ is the system size. This bound shows that OaRC achieves asymptotic optimality for overloaded systems when the system size $N$ scales to infinity. Moreover, the bound is independent of the state-space size, which is a desirable property when job states contain contextual information. We corroborate our results with an extensive simulation study based on two holding cost patterns (online ads and user-generated content) that arise in content moderation for social media platforms. Our simulations based on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that OaRC consistently outperforms existing practice, which is based on the two canonical algorithmic principles.

papers.name: Degenerate symplectic fixed points and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Gromov--Witten invariants and the number of fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed rational symplectic manifolds, without assuming nondegeneracy, via deformed Hamiltonian spectral invariants. We obtain a Hamiltonian fixed point estimate involving Gromov--Witten invariants with one point insertion under an explicit minimum-area hypothesis. We propose three conjectures about Hamiltonian fixed point estimate and prove them for every generalized flag manifold $X=G/P$ equipped with a rational Kähler form. We extend Schwarz's quantum cuplength to deformed quantum cuplength for symplectic periods and use it to obtain estimates on monotone symplectic manifolds admitting nonzero mixed Gromov--Witten invariants. We use the quantum-factorization estimate to recover the Fano toric case of Givental's symplectic fixed-point theorem. Finally, a graded spectral-carrier argument gives uniform fixed-point bounds on negatively monotone manifolds.

papers.name: The uncertainty of a tournament draw: Insights from the Champions League
papers.abstract: The group draw of major sports tournaments implies some uncertainty, with lucky teams often enjoying a substantial unfair advantage. For the first time in the literature, we propose a technique to quantify this draw uncertainty, which, arguably, should be minimised. Our simulation-based approach requires generating a representative set of random draws to compute the variance of qualifying probabilities for each team. The method is applied to compare draw uncertainty in the former group stage and the current incomplete round-robin league phase of the UEFA Champions League, under both accurate and inaccurate seedings. We also break down the impact of the 2024/25 reform into various components. The new format is found to decrease draw uncertainty, but the reduction is mainly attributable to the inaccurate seeding system used by UEFA. Consequently, the primary benefit of an incomplete round-robin tournament compared to the standard group stage lies in the robustness of its draw uncertainty to the seeding of the teams.

papers.name: Beta representations with minimal mean digit
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of minimising the mean digit in beta representations with unrestricted digits, equivalent to a one dimensional affine switched system obtained from a formal limit of a stabilisable two dimensional linear system. We give a countable set of $β$ for which the result is given by the usual (greedy) beta expansion, an interval of values for which it is strictly less, a numerical upper bound, and a conditional lower bound for all $β$.

papers.name: A geometric perspective on Amitsur's conjecture
papers.abstract: Amitsur proved that Severi--Brauer varieties associated with cyclic algebras of the same degree are birationally equivalent whenever their Brauer classes generate the same cyclic subgroup. We give a geometric proof of this result by constructing explicit birational maps in homogeneous coordinates and using Galois descent.

papers.name: Equivalent bounded confidence processes
papers.abstract: In the bounded confidence model the opinions of a set of agents evolve over discrete time steps. In each round an agent averages the opinion of all agents whose opinions are at most a certain threshold apart. Here we assume that the opinions of the agents are elements of the real line. The details of the dynamics are determined by the initial opinions of the agents, i.e. a starting configuration, and the mentioned threshold -- both admitting uncountably many possibilities. Recently it was conjectured that for each starting configuration the set of thresholds can be partitioned into a finite number of intervals such that the evolution of opinions does not depend on the precise value of the threshold within one of the intervals. So, we may say that, given a starting configuration of initial opinions, there is only a finite number of equivalence classes of bounded confidence processes (and an algorithm to compute them). Here we systematically study different notions of equivalence. Under our broadest notion of equivalence we can also get rid of the initial starting configuration and end up with a finite number of equivalent bounded confidence processes for each given (finite) number of agents. This allows to precisely study the occurring phenomena for small numbers of agents without the jeopardy of missing interesting cases by performing numerical experiments. We exemplarily study the freezing time, i.e. number of time steps needed until the process stabilizes, and the degree of fragmentation, i.e. the number of different opinions that survive once the process has reached its final state.

papers.name: On subradically sifted sums related to Alladi's higher order duality between prime factors
papers.abstract: In this paper, I utilize a variant of the Selberg--Delange method to find quantitative estimates of the sums \[M_{k,ω}(x,y)=\sum_{\substack{p_{1}(n)> y\\ n\leq x} } μ(n) {ω(n)-1\choose k-1},\] where $y$ can grow with $x$ but we must have $y\leq Y_0\exp(\mathscr{p}\frac{\log x}{(\log\log (x+1))^{1+ε}})$ with $Y_0,\mathscr{p},ε>0$. Moreover, I give preliminary upper bounds for the general range $1.9\leq y\leq x^{\frac{1}{k}}$. In addition, I formalize the notions of subradical and radical dominance and discuss their relevance to the analytic approach to the study of arithmetic functions. Lastly, I give a fascinating formula related to the derivatives of the gamma function and the Hankel contour, which should be relevant for those employing the Selberg--Delange method to obtain higher-order terms.

papers.name: Global smoothing of singular Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties
papers.abstract: We study the problem of smoothing Fano and Calabi-Yau varieties with isolated Du Bois (equivalently, log canonical) lci singularities. For Fano varieties, we show that any such $Y$ admits a deformation to a Fano variety with only $1$-rational singularities, and if $Y$ has only non-$1$-rational hypersurface singularities, then $Y$ is smoothable. For Calabi-Yau varieties, we show first that any such $Y$ deforms to a Calabi-Yau with only $1$-Du Bois singularities. Moreover, if $Y$ has only non-$1$-Du Bois hypersurface singularities then $Y$ is smoothable. Both smoothing statements extend to lci singularities satisfying suitable local conditions. When we allow a Calabi-Yau to have $1$-liminal singularities, a global condition is needed, which we express in terms of the Hodge-Du Bois numbers of $Y$. These theorems recover and generalize results for threefolds of Friedman, Namikawa, Namikawa-Steenbrink, Gross, and Friedman-Laza. In higher dimensions, our results provide alternative smoothing conditions and also extend the work of Friedman-Laza from the case of rational hypersurface singularities to Du Bois lci singularities.

papers.name: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
papers.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

papers.name: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.name: Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calderón problem
papers.abstract: We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calderón problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.

papers.name: Axioms for validity: from tests, e-values and p-values to decisions
papers.abstract: The emerging literature on hypothesis testing with data-dependent significance levels relies on a particular extension of the Type-I error. Existing arguments for this extension are heuristic. We show it is uniquely characterized by three axioms: law-invariance, agreement with classical testing on constant levels, and the preservation of (in)validity under independent selection of the level. We find that three analogous axioms characterize the e-value as a multi-decision generalization of a test. We also characterize the p-value, reducing the p-vs-e debate to a simple property: should independent selection among evidence variables that are invalid under the same null distribution be able to produce a valid evidence variable? Our main technical contribution is to show how e-values emerge in every decision problem with a notion of validity that satisfies law invariance, the independent selection axiom, and an axiom stating that a procedure that selects an invalid procedure with arbitrarily high probability must itself be invalid. We also extend recent results using e-values to support decision making to arbitrary evidence variables. In an application, we justify expectation-based error rates in multiple testing and recover the 'e-closure principle'.

papers.name: A high-order IMEX-DG solver for atmospheric dynamics: rotating tests on non-conforming meshes
papers.abstract: We present a high-order implicit-explicit discontinuous Galerkin (IMEX-DG) solver for the compressible Euler equations that accounts for rotational effects within an atmospheric framework. Time integration follows a second-order additive Runge-Kutta scheme, treating stiff acoustic modes implicitly and advective terms explicitly. The solver is built on the deal.II finite element library, combining matrix-free operator evaluation, adaptive non-conforming mesh capabilities, and distributed-memory parallelism. The inclusion of rotation extends the framework to large-scale atmospheric dynamics, where the Coriolis force plays a central role in geostrophic balance. Its incorporation into a high-order matrix-free DG discretisation is, however, non-trivial, as it requires a careful formulation of the discrete rotational operator. Two alternative treatments of the rotational and gravitational source terms within the solution strategy, based on nonlinear fixed-point iterations, are therefore introduced and compared in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. A discrete analysis of the rotational operator is also carried out in order to derive a formulation suitable for efficient matrix-free implementation. The proposed formulation is verified through convergence studies on rotating inertia-gravity wave benchmarks and further assessed in fully three-dimensional simulations of stratified flow over orography on both uniform and adaptive meshes. The numerical results show that the rotating IMEX-DG framework has the expected accuracy and stability properties while correctly capturing the asymmetry and wave structures induced by rotation in large-scale atmospheric flows.

papers.name: On $H=W$ in Banach function spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove ``$H=W$" in the context of a Banach function space $X(Ω)$. Let $Ω$ be a subset of ${\mathbb R}^n$ and denote by $W^1_X(Ω)$ the collection of all those $f\in X(Ω)$ whose distributional derivatives $\partial_jf$ are contained in $X(Ω)$. Our main result provides a small collection of ``universal" hypotheses on $X(Ω)$ that ensure $W^1_X(Ω)$ is equal to $H^1_X(Ω)$, the formal closure of ${Lip}(Ω)\cap W^1_X(Ω)$ with respect to the norm \[\|f\|_{W^1_X(Ω)} = \|f\|_{X(Ω)} + \|\nabla f\|_{X(Ω)}.\] The main theorem has two corollaries. The first gives a slightly stronger set of hypotheses for ``$H=W$", and the second gives density of $C^\infty_c({\mathbb R}^n)$ in $W^1_X({\mathbb R}^n)$.

papers.name: Birational Algebraic Topology
papers.abstract: Over any qcqs scheme $S$, we show that inverting dense open immersions in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, $log\mbox{-}\mathcal{H}^\Box(S)$, and $\mathcal{P}_Σ(\mathrm{Sm}_S)$ yields the same birational $\infty$-category $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$. Unlike in $\mathcal{H}^{\mathbb{A}^1}(S)$, all Nisnevich truncations and homotopy sheaves (including $π_0^{nis}$) of birational spaces remain birational, and hence $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is Postnikov complete. Moreover, the birational localization $L_{bir}$ commutes with the bar construction, ensuring effective delooping for every grouplike object in $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ and yielding an unstable birational higher-connectivity theorem. Building on these results, we establish birational analogs of the van Kampen theorem, the higher Galois theory of coverings, and the Freudenthal suspension theorem. When $S$ is geometrically unibranch with finitely many generic points, we show that $\mathcal{H}^b(S)$ is in fact an $\infty$-topos of homotopy dimension zero. Over a perfect field, we identify discrete birational group sheaves with strongly $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant sheaves whose $\mathbb{G}_m$-contraction vanishes, and deduce that $S^{2,1}$-nullification $L^{2,1}$ agrees with $L_{bir}$ on pointed $L^{2,1}$-connected spaces. Finally, over any field, we prove that $L_{bir}$ preserves generic values of $π_0^{\mathbb{A}^1}$ on motivic colimits of proper schemes; over perfect fields, it therefore detects their $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectivity and yields an equivalence $\mathbb{H}_0^{\mathbb{A}^1} \simeq \mathbb{H}_0^b$ for them, answering a question of Asok and Haesemeyer in greater generality.

papers.name: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$, and let $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra. For central division $F$-algebras $L$ of fixed degree $n$, the double quotients $L^\times\backslash L_E^\times/L^\times$ are identified with a common topological space $\widehatΞ_E$. Each $L$ gives a convolution product $*_E^L$ on the space ${\mathcal M}_E$ of compactly supported measures on $\widehatΞ_E$. The first conjecture asserts that this product is independent of $L$. I prove it for split $E$ and, for every $E$, in degrees $1,2,3,4,6$. The second part of the article defines geometric Hecke operators $T_D^L$ for finite étale divisors $D$ of ${\mathbb P}^1_F$ disjoint from the level divisor, and identifies their convolution measures $μ_D^L\in{\mathcal M}_E$. The second conjecture asserts that these measures are independent of $L$.

papers.name: The number of composite class sizes in finite groups
papers.abstract: We consider finite groups with at least three conjugacy class sizes that are composite numbers and we prove that, in that situation, the number of prime class sizes is bounded by the number of composite class sizes. The analogous result for (non-)prime-power class sizes is also addressed.

papers.name: Non-vanishing uniqueness threshold for hyperbolic Poisson-Voronoi percolation in dimension at least three
papers.abstract: We study the threshold for the existence of exactly one unbounded cluster for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the $d$-dimensional hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d$ for $d\geq 3$. By recent results of Grebík and Recke and d'Achille et al., this "uniqueness threshold" $p_u(λ)$ tends to zero as the intensity $λ$ of the underlying Poisson point process tends to zero, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation defined on an ambient space from a family of geometric spaces that includes Cartesian products $\mathbb{H}^{d_1}\times\dots\times\mathbb{H}^{d_k}$ with $k,d_1,\dots,d_k\geq 2$. In contrast, for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}^2$, Benjamini and Schramm have shown that $p_u(λ)$ tends to one as $λ$ tends to zero, and $p_u(λ)>1/2$ for all $λ>0$. An unpublished argument of D'Achille and Curien shows that for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$, the uniqueness threshold satisfies $p_u(λ)\leq 1/2$ for all $λ>0$. Here we will show that $\inf_{λ>0}p_u(λ)>0$ for Poisson-Voronoi percolation on $\mathbb{H}^d$ with $d\geq 3$. This answers a question of Grebík and Recke. The ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is a random tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^d$ introduced recently by D'Achille et al. In a sense that can be made precise, it corresponds to the $λ\searrow 0$ limit of the Poisson-Voronoi tessellation. Via a minor adaptation of our proof, we are also able to show that the uniqueness threshold of the ideal Poisson-Voronoi tessellation is strictly positive.

papers.name: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
papers.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

papers.name: The least-squares RBF-PU method for linear elasticity in the diaphragm geometry
papers.abstract: The human diaphragm is vital for respiration and its simulation can aid in further understanding complications arising in individuals that have been subjected to mechanical ventilation. The diaphragm is very thin and hence its numerical simulation poses a challenge for most numerical methods. In this paper, we compute the deformation of real diaphragm geometries, which are modelled as linear elastic, and are subject to realistic boundary conditions. The method used is the unfitted least-squares radial basis function partition of unity method. The patches used are cylindrical and refinement is performed along the thin direction of the diaphragm. Both the unfitted nature of the method as well as the refinement technique make this method particularly well suited to solve problems formulated in thin geometries. We derive a theoretical proof showing that the method converges with high order to the solution of a well-posed linear elasticity boundary value problem.

papers.name: Auslander correspondence for higher stable dg categories and cluster Morita theory
papers.abstract: We prove a cluster Morita theorem: every pretriangulated dg category with a $d$-cluster tilting subcategory is realized as the $d$-cluster dg category of that subcategory regarded as a connective dg category. Reversing the Amiot--Guo construction, this yields a bijection between $d$-stable dg categories and pretriangulated dg categories with a chosen $d$-cluster tilting subcategory. Our Auslander correspondence characterizes $d$-stability by coherence, weak global dimension at most $d+1$, and a $(d+1)$-shifted duality on finitely presented modules. For a locally finite $d$-stable dg algebra over a field, right $(d+1)$-Calabi--Yau structures on its perfectly valued derived dg category correspond bijectively to right $d$-Calabi--Yau structures on its $d$-cluster dg category. In characteristic zero, this removes the pseudo-compact enhancement hypothesis from Keller--Liu's theorem on Amiot's conjecture. Via Koszul duality, we characterize $d$-stability over any field for locally finite minimal completed dg path algebras (and their analogues for graded species) by explicit conditions on the graded arrows and the quadratic differential. For $d=1$, these are deformed derived mesh algebras of Dynkin type; for $d=2$, they are complete twisted Ginzburg dg algebras, yielding via cluster Morita theory a twisted analogue of Amiot's conjecture in arbitrary characteristic without a Calabi--Yau hypothesis.

papers.name: Quasilinear multiplication in the Cayley-Dickson tower
papers.abstract: Direct evaluation of the defining product of the Cayley-Dickson algebra $A_n$ of rank $N:=2^n$ requires a quadratic number of arithmetic operations. This paper gives a uniform bilinear algorithm that computes multiplication in $A_n$ over a unital commutative ring $R$ in which $2\in R^\times$ using $O(N\log N)$ arithmetic operations and $O(N)$ auxiliary storage, given $A_n$ is defined with doubling parameters that are units with square roots in a fixed commutative algebra finitely generated as an $R$-module admitting a linear surjection onto the base ring preserving the identity. These conditions are satisfied by every Cayley-Dickson tower over $\mathbb{R}$ and over finite fields of odd characteristic, where the tensor rank of multiplication in $A_n$ is at most $(36n-69)2^{n-3}+10$ for $n\ge4$. To the author's knowledge, this is the first uniform subquadratic algorithm for multiplication in $A_n$. In single-core benchmarks over $\mathbb{R}$, an open-source implementation in the library fastCD is approximately $17$ times faster than direct multiplication at $N=1024$.

papers.name: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
papers.abstract: We study gradient descent with predetermined nonnegative stepsizes on smooth strongly convex functions. Let $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)$ and $κ$ be the condition number. We prove the iteration lower bound $Ω\left(κ^{\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{sil}}}-o(1)}\log\frac1δ\right)$ for both relative squared distance and relative function error, uniformly over $0<δ<1$ and sufficiently large $κ$. This matches the polynomial exponent of $κ$ for the Silver stepsize schedule established in [Altschuler and Parrilo, 2025].

papers.name: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

papers.name: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support Kähler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

papers.name: Nowhere Locally Metric-Minimising Saddle Surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the relation between the saddle property and local metric minimality for smooth surfaces in Euclidean spaces. Anton Petrunin and Stephan Stadler proved that every smooth strictly saddle surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is locally metric-minimising and expressed the expectation that this phenomenon fails in $\mathbb{R}^4$. We confirm this expectation and prove a stronger density result: Every smooth strictly saddle embedding of a closed disc into $\mathbb{R}^4$ can be approximated arbitrarily closely in the $C^\infty$-topology by smooth strictly saddle embeddings that are nowhere locally metric-minimising. In particular, nowhere locally metric-minimising saddle embeddings exist in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for every $d \geq 4$. The main ingredient is the construction of non-trivial infinitesimal isometric deformations of saddle immersions in $\mathbb{R}^4$ supported in arbitrarily small discs. We also provide an explicit twisted quadratic surface that is saddle in a neighbourhood of the origin but fails to be locally metric-minimising there, by deriving a necessary condition for metric minimality.

papers.name: Nearly Sharp Uniform Projection Bounds and Superlinear Vitushkin Inequalities for Deterministic Self-Similar Sets
papers.abstract: For all integers $1 \le k < d$ and every $α\in (0,1)$, we construct an explicit deterministic finite homogeneous iterated function system of similarities in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space satisfying the open set condition. The same system is used at every scale. Its attractor $F_{k,α}$ has positive and finite $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Write $A_δ$ for the closed $δ$-neighbourhood of a set $A$. For all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, every orthogonal projection of $(F_{k,α})_δ$ onto a $k$-plane has $k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure at most $C_{k,α}(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$. The construction places the product of a planar self-similar set $E_α$ and the unit $(k-1)$-cube in a coordinate $(k+1)$-plane. For every $0 < δ< 1$, the supremum of these projected measures is comparable, up to constants depending only on $k$, to the supremum of the lengths of the orthogonal projections of $(E_α)_δ$ onto lines. We bound this latter supremum by $C_α(\log(1/δ))^{-α}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$. We also prove that the analytic capacity $γ((E_α)_δ)$ is comparable to $(\log(1/δ))^{-1/2}$ for all sufficiently small $δ> 0$, with constants depending only on $α$. Consequently, the Favard length of $(E_α)_δ$ is at most $C_αγ((E_α)_δ)^{2α}$ for every $0 < δ< 1$. This quantitative Vitushkin inequality is superlinear for $α> 1/2$, and its exponent $2α$ approaches the optimal upper limit of two for this class of self-similar sets as $α$ tends to one.

papers.name: Rigidity and deformations of Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We generalize Zoll families of hypersurfaces to Besse families of hypersurfaces, which are defined differential-topologically and may contain non-embedded and exceptional hypersurfaces. A contact-geometric discussion presents them as double Legendrian fibrations and shows that regular hypersurfaces are either spheres or real projective spaces. In analogy with the Berger conjecture on simply connected manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed, we show that every hypersurface of a Besse family on a closed manifold is regular. On even-dimensional manifolds we obtain a stronger conclusion, generalizing a theorem of Gromoll and Grove about 2-spheres all of whose geodesics are closed: every hypersurface of a Besse family is regular and embedded. Moreover, building on work by Ambrozio and Guajardo, we provide metrics with trivial isometry group carrying Zoll families of non-embedded minimal hypersurfaces in every odd dimension at least three, and Besse families of minimal hypersurfaces with exceptional hypersurfaces on orbifolds in every dimension at least two. We also give a short proof that manifolds admitting Zoll families of embedded hypersurfaces are homeomorphic to spheres or real projective spaces, recovering a recent result of Martins up to homeomorphism. In particular, this applies to all even-dimensional manifolds with a Besse family.

papers.name: On the symplectic cohomology of orbifold divisor complements
papers.abstract: This article studies the symplectic cohomology of Liouville domains whose contact boundaries admit a periodic Reeb flow, with a particular focus on affine varieties which arise as orbifold divisor complements. We describe a formula for the Conley-Zehnder indices which allows for a simple determination of the positive equivariant symplectic cohomology in cases when the inertia orbifold of the compactifying divisor has only even degree cohomology. This is then applied to the study of orbifold compactifications of $\mathbb{C}^n$. Moreover, we analyse the action of multiplication by the principal orbit on V-shaped symplectic cohomology and prove that if the compactification $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{D})$ is positively monotone, then this class induces a periodic structure on symplectic cohomology, reducing the problem of computing an infinite-dimensional group to a finite-dimensional repeating portion. We combine the index computations and this periodic structure to compute the symplectic cohomology of various Milnor fibers of surface singularities, the rational homology balls $B_{p,q}$ as well as ample divisor complements in orbifold K3 surfaces and Calabi-Yau threefolds, which includes the Milnor fibers of the exceptional unimodal singularities.

papers.name: Quadratic Elements in Finite $p$-Groups and Applications to Oliver's $p$-Group Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish a property of quadratic elements in faithful modules for finite $p$-groups. Let $p$ be an odd prime, and suppose that $a$ is a quadratic element of an abelian subgroup $L$ normalized by $b$. Writing $a_0=a$ and $a_i=[a_{i-1},b]$, we prove that if, for some $r$ with $2\leq r\leq(p+1)/2$, one has $a_{r-1}\neq1$ and $a_r=1$, then $a_{r-1}$ is quadratic. As an application, we verify the Weakly Closed Conjecture for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $p+2$, and hence establish the Quadratic Conjecture for these groups. Consequently, Oliver's $p$-group conjecture holds for a finite $p$-group $S$ whenever $S/\mathfrak X(S)$ has nilpotency class at most $p+2$.

papers.name: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
papers.abstract: We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

papers.name: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

papers.name: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
papers.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

papers.name: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

papers.name: On the $φ^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
papers.abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $φ^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.

papers.name: Steinness and Complete Expanding Kähler-Ricci Solitons
